event.summary: Voters in five states—Michigan, Virginia, Missouri, Kansas, and Washington—are heading to the polls for primary elections. Observers are particularly focused on the Democratic Senate showdown in Michigan and other significant contests in the participating states.

event_overview.title: About US Primaries
event_overview.subject: US Primaries
event_overview.summary: U.S. primaries are state-administered elections held before the November general election to select or narrow the field of candidates for public office. The August 4, 2026 contests are part of the midterm-election cycle, but their rules and ballot formats differ by state.

facts.label: Date and states
facts.value: Kansas, Michigan, Missouri, Washington and Virginia hold 2026 primary elections on August 4; Arizona's 2026 primary was held earlier, on July 21.

facts.label: General-election link
facts.value: The candidates or finalists emerging from these contests proceed toward the November 3, 2026 general election, subject to each state's ballot-access and election rules.

facts.label: State-specific formats
facts.value: Primary systems are not uniform: Missouri voters may choose a party ballot, while Washington uses a top-two primary in which the two highest vote-getters for an office advance regardless of party preference.

facts.label: Administration and certification
facts.value: Election administration is decentralized through state and local election authorities; for example, Washington counties canvass August-primary results before statewide certification, while Michigan publishes its own election calendar and results through the Secretary of State.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on notable August 4 primary developments and selected high-profile races across five states, not a complete record of every primary contest, local ballot measure, result, recount, or U.S. election event.
